kind: consistency / hand-rolled parse replaceable by shared idiom
title: row_limit parses with raw parseInt(v) (no radix) instead of the imported safeParseInt helper
description: The row-limit onChange uses `Math.max(0, parseInt(v) || 0)`. `parseInt` is called with no radix argument (a lint-flagged smell) and re-implements NaN-handling via `|| 0`, even though `safeParseInt(raw, fallback)` is already imported at the top of this very file (line 3) and is used a few lines above for the seed input (line 86: `safeParseInt(e.target.value, 42)`). Replacing with `Math.max(0, safeParseInt(v, 0))` removes the missing-radix smell and matches the established idiom. This is the same finding-class already catalogued for another editor (review/04-exhaustive/raw/frontend-b1.json:1508, the GLMFactorConfig `df` field), so it is a recognised cleanup pattern in this repo.
evidence: Line 181: `onUpdate("row_limit", v === "" ? null : Math.max(0, parseInt(v) || 0));` — note `parseInt` has no radix arg and `|| 0` re-rolls NaN-safety. Compare line 86 (seed): `safeParseInt(e.target.value, 42)`. `safeParseInt` is defined utils/configField.ts:26-29 as `parseInt(raw, 10)` with NaN fallback, and is already imported on line 3. Behaviour is identical for all values a `type=number` input can emit (parseInt and parseInt(.,10) differ only on `0x`/legacy-octal prefixes the input rejects).
est_reduction: ~1 line simplified; removes one missing-radix lint smell and one duplicated NaN-guard
behavior_preservation: Behaviour-preserving for all inputs a numeric input field can produce; both paths yield the same integer and the same 0 fallback.
